band.advice.critical: Hand off now. The context is effectively full, so the next thing this session forgets may be something you still need.
band.advice.high: Hand off soon. There is not much room left, and what gets dropped to make room is the earliest context - usually the goal and the constraints.
band.advice.unknown: No content could be read, so there is nothing to judge the remaining room from. This transcript is a compressed archive (Codex compresses rollouts after 7 days) and no zstd decompressor is available here. Installing either one restores full triage: Python 3.14 ships compression.zstd, or pip install zstandard.
band.advice.watch: Safe to continue, but keep an eye on it: past this point a long detour can fill the rest in one go.
band.basis.size: estimated from file size (no token count in the transcript; error is large - a compacted session is smaller precisely because it dropped more)
band.basis.tokens: {tokens} tokens used (the transcript does not state a context limit, so absolute thresholds apply)
band.basis.unreadable: not a single line of content could be read, so nothing can be judged
band.floor.compactions: compacted {count} time(s) - raised to "{floor}". Compaction only fires when it no longer fits, so having compacted means having been full.
band.raised: The final band comes from a raise rule, not from the primary basis above.

doctor.lead: This tool fails silently almost every time: something is missing from the environment and the result is not an error but an empty column, or a batch of sessions that never shows up. This states those up front.

doc.vitals.basis: Ranked by how full each session's context is. The number comes from the transcript itself - Claude records `message.usage`, Codex records a `token_count` event that also carries the model's limit - so it is measured, not guessed. A session that has already compacted is treated as having hit the limit, because automatic compaction only fires when the context can no longer fit; each compaction drops older history. File size is only the fallback for transcripts that record no token counts: size and real usage come apart badly, and a small file can mean compaction has been discarding history all along.
doc.vitals.head: | Agent | Session | Context | Size | Fatal | Aborted | Tool errors | Verdict |

The working directory, repositories and transcript path shown below belong to that machine, so they will not resolve here - and it cannot be resumed natively, because the app only indexes sessions in its own data directory. Its content is still worth carrying over: tick it and generate a handoff.
gui.tip.fullness: {pct}% of the context window used - {tokens} of {window} tokens. This, not file size, is what the verdict is based on.
gui.tip.resume: {cmd} - resuming natively in the original app keeps most of what a handoff cannot carry: tool approvals, the reasoning behind rejected approaches, the full conversation history. It is not lossless, though: Anthropic has documented full prompt-cache misses on the first request after a resume, MCP tools that an older session referenced being retired since, background tasks becoming orphaned, and the resume semantics of model selection changing between releases. Prefer this whenever the session is intact and you are on the same machine, then check /model and your background tasks once it comes back.

gui.tip.unreadable: This transcript is a compressed archive - Codex automatically compresses sessions older than 7 days into .jsonl.zst - and no zstd decompressor is available here, so not a single line of content was read. The vitals, digest and verbatim asks are all empty; that does not mean the session is clean. Installing either one restores full reading: Python 3.14 ships compression.zstd, or pip install zstandard.
